findings.text: Mapping write exclusion uses paired helpers around the address space interval semaphore. One helper acquires write ownership and the other releases it. The hugetlb scan hole path holds this write ownership outside huge page table locking, defining an outer to inner nesting order.

Hugetlb hole write protection works at huge page granularity across the requested interval. Allocation failure is reported as out of memory and success is reported otherwise. Empty entries require no translation flush while entries that became populated during setup receive a range flush for that huge page.
An alternate build disables hugetlb scan support by defining the hugetlb entry callback as absent and making the hole write protection helper a successful no operation over any interval.

Scan hole handling is a successful no operation when no area is present. For present areas the emitted category derives from current area state with an added written mark for userfault write protected non hugetlb areas. Only interesting ranges are emitted, with optional write protection applied through hugetlb or generic range handling and protection failures propagated.
Scan walk dispatch associates walk testing, middle level entries, holes, and hugetlb entries with their respective scan handlers in a single operation table.

User scan arguments are accepted only with matching structure size, flags and category masks within supported sets, untagged addresses, page aligned start, accessible address and vector ranges, and consistent vector presence and length. End is rounded upward to page granularity, walk progress starts cleared, and an absent page limit means unlimited.

Result staging uses a bounded kernel buffer sized by walk chunk and remaining vector capacity with output position tracking the user vector. Flushing copies completed ranges to user space, advances accounting, and resets for reuse. Completion writes back only walk progress to the user arguments.

Scan execution covers argument validation, buffer setup, interruptible ranged walking under read protection with optional protection notifications, buffer flushing with range counting, and final accounting with writeback and release. Buffer full and limit reached conditions end with a range count rather than an error, while signals, lock interruption, and copy failures end with errors.

Control dispatch routes the scan command to the scan implementation using the file private address space and rejects other commands. The pagemap file interface exposes seek, read, open, release, and native plus compat control dispatch through the same handler.
Visible interfaces for other units include pagemap, NUMA maps, and no MMU maps file operation tables and a registration routine for vmcore device memory callbacks.

NUMA accounting aggregates total, anonymous, active, writeback, dirty, swap cache, maximum sharing, and per node page counts. Private iterator state pairs generic maps iteration context with one such aggregate.

Per page NUMA accounting records dirtiness, swap cache membership, activity including unevictable status, writeback, anonymity, sharing peak, and node placement. Eligibility excludes non present entries, non normal or device or reserved pages, and pages outside online memory nodes.

NUMA collection treats transparent huge pages as a single aggregate and otherwise iterates base pages under table locking with scheduling cooperation. Huge entry collection under huge table locking is either a present gated single page aggregate or a successful no operation in the alternate build.

NUMA walk configuration provides read locked and verified area locked variants sharing entry handlers. Selection uses the read locked variant when the iterator already holds address space protection, with an alternate build always using the read locked variant.

NUMA maps sequential output reports policy, backing association with heap stack and huge markers, collected counters with per node breakdown and kernel page size, skipping page walking for the gate area while temporarily dropping read protection. Iteration uses standard start next stop show operations with an open sizing private state.

No MMU maps output renders address bounds, permission characters, offset, device numbers, inode, and backing path or stack marker. Sequential iteration uses start next stop show operations with open establishing private state and memory reference and release dropping them.

No MMU iteration pins the target task and address space and holds read protection across traversal. Start handles absent task, dead memory, and interruptible acquisition, while stop releases task, memory reference, and read protection. Position advances by area start with a distinct terminal value.

Thread self link resolution reports current thread group and thread identifiers in hierarchical form, using allocation mode suited to calling context with registered cleanup. The inode interface exposes only link resolution, with a globally assigned inode number.

Uptime output combines per CPU idle totals with boot time adjusted for time namespace and presents both as fixed precision seconds. Version output presents system name, release, and version from system identity. Both entries are created as permanent single show proc files during initialization.

Crash dump state includes core buffer with current and original sizes, notes buffer with current and original sizes, total dump size with proc entry, device dump list nodes carrying buffer and length, and flags for device dump disablement plus open tracking. Logging uses a fixed vmcore prefix.

Callback list mutation and late registration handling are serialized by a dedicated mutex. Registration appends to the tail, warns once on post open registration, and immediately processes device memory when no open is active and the callback provides a handler, all under the same hold.

Device memory incorporation accepts only 64 bit dumps, ignores empty range sets and overlapping registrations, and on success transfers ownership of new ranges without freeing them while freeing on failure or overlap. Range acquisition failures are logged without further action.

Scan hazards include faults on inaccessible user memory, invalid requests on size flag mask alignment or vector mismatch, interruption on pending fatal signals or killed lock acquisition, and faults on result copyback. Early stop and limit conditions are reported as counts rather than errors.

NUMA display must skip the gate area and must drop and reacquire read protection around potentially sleeping walks. Device range handling must reject non 64 bit dumps and overlapping registrations to avoid duplicate accounting.
Scan control uses a dedicated scan command with a fixed size argument structure, page size alignment, supported flag and category mask sets, and a write match option gating protection notifications.
